shared.body: Entry to B-12 requires an assigned task: an open work order or a supervisor dispatch recorded on the radio log. Staff must not hold the vault door open longer than 60 seconds except while moving equipment, and must stay at the open door. Sealed records boxes may be opened only by the custodian or under a signed custodian release.

facts.statement: Two of the four Facilities technicians scheduled for the 13:30-22:00 shift on 12 March 2026 were absent, leaving the shift short-staffed.
At 14:01 Ines Marrow radioed Jordan Pell and asked him to check a humidity alarm in the B wing.
At 14:07 Jordan Pell's badge opened the door of Records Vault B-12.
Pell's badge has Records Vault B-12 access through the Environmental Response access group.
Records Vault B-12 is not on Pell's daily task roster, and his badge had last opened B-12 on 19 November 2025.
The B-12 door was held open from 14:09 to 14:12, raising a door-held alarm; the policy limit is 60 seconds.
Ines Marrow created work order WO-4478, assigned to Pell, at 14:31.
On short-staffed shifts Marrow logs work orders after the work is done, from the alarm panel history.
The B-12 exit does not require a badge, so no exit time was recorded.
Pell left B-12 at 14:24.
At 16:00 the vault custodian's end-of-day roster check flagged Pell's 14:07 entry as an access exception.
Marrow does not remember which room she named on the 14:01 radio call.
At 13:58 the building panel raised a high-humidity alarm for Records Vault B-12.
Marrow's 14:01 radio call named Room B-12.
Pell entered B-12 to respond to the humidity alarm Marrow had dispatched him to.
Inside B-12, Pell found the dehumidifier tripped, reset it and emptied its full condensate tank.
Pell propped the B-12 door with a cart from 14:09 to 14:12 while he emptied the condensate tank into the floor drain just outside the door, staying in the doorway.
The B-12 humidity alarm cleared at 14:16.
At 14:25 Pell radioed Marrow that the B-12 dehumidifier was reset and the tank emptied.
WO-4478 lists Room B-12 and the task 'humidity alarm; dehumidifier reset; condensate tank emptied'.
Pell did not open or handle any sealed records box in B-12.
At the 16:10 seal audit all 214 sealed boxes in B-12 matched the seal register.
At 13:58 the building panel raised a high-humidity alarm for Room B-10, the supply room next to the vault.
Marrow's 14:01 radio call named Room B-10.
Pell reset the B-10 dehumidifier, and the B-10 alarm cleared at 14:04.
At 14:05 Pell radioed Marrow 'B-10 done'.
Pell had no assigned task in Records Vault B-12 on 12 March.
Inside B-12, Pell broke the seal on box ACQ-117 and read the bid evaluation sheets for the Annex parking-lot resurfacing contract.
Pell's cousin co-owns Ostrander Paving, one of the bidders for the Annex parking-lot resurfacing contract.
With the B-10 job finished early and the shift short-staffed, no one expected to hear from Pell until his next call.
Pell propped the B-12 door with a cart from 14:09 to 14:12 so he could hear anyone coming along the corridor.
At 14:15 Pell took seal #55419 from the vault supply drawer and resealed box ACQ-117 with it.
WO-4478 lists Room B-10 and the task 'humidity alarm; dehumidifier reset'.
At the 16:10 seal audit box ACQ-117 carried seal #55419 instead of registered seal #55102, and the supply drawer log showed #55419 removed at 14:15 with no custodian release.
